commit.message:
feat(forge-tracker): offer label setup on first use

An unconfigured repo now gets one setup: line per report instead of several
parenthetical notes, and /next says when its empty queue only means no label
is configured. forge-tracker labels suggest reads the repo labels and prints a
proposed .claude/forge-tracker.local.md; labels decline remembers a no in the
local cache. A label or ruling_pattern set to ~ records that the repo has none
and silences the line. The commands offer setup once and write the config
file only on the user yes; missing labels stay gh commands for the user.

Closes #59

commit.message:
feat(session-decisions): per-repo forge override in git config (tracker.forge, tracker.web)

A clone can name the forge its references link to with `git config tracker.forge <kind>` and `git config tracker.web <https URL>`. The override wins over forge_hosts and the built-in host rules, which covers SSH host aliases, mirrors whose issues live elsewhere, and SSH hosts that differ from the web host. A web base under a subpath links GitHub and Forgejo references there. Values the plugin cannot use are named in a toast at session start. Without an override, the remote decides as before.

fix(forge-tracker): list open PRs with no open issue in /next

every other one, and its facts carried no PR data of their own. A PR

commit.message:
fix(session-decisions): accept (recommend: ...) and nested parentheses at any depth

The TaskCreate hook required whitespace straight after "recommend", so a
subject written as "(recommend: <choice>)" was refused as having no
recommendation. Accept the colon form too.

The choice is now found by matching the closing parenthesis by depth
instead of a regex that allowed one nested level, so a choice with deeper
nesting keeps its Accept button and recommends tag. The card's short tag
cuts at the first comma or semicolon outside parentheses.

Fixes #27

response.body: Four commands-and-layer tickets filed as parts of this plugin: #21 (read-only forge layer for GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo), #23 (/catchup), #24 (/next), #22 (/groom).

Progress, 2026-10-16:
- Done for GitHub: the read layer (#41), `/catchup` (#23, closed), `/next` (#24, closed), first-use label setup (#59, closed).
- Under way: `/groom` (#22).
- Still to do: the phase-2 working rules and hooks, and the GitLab and Forgejo adapters (#21).
- Open: unlabeled repos producing an empty `/next` queue (#69).

Rule to build in: any issue assigned to a person, and any comment asking one, carries an explicit ask line, for example "@user, the ask: <answer this / verify with these steps / investigate / attach>". The write path should refuse a question comment with no mention and no ask. Without it, people end up asking "what is needed from me?" on items that a keyword flagged for them.

## Survey: OpenCode (step 1) Tested against OpenCode **1.19.4** (npm `opencode-ai`, the current `latest`), installed into a scratch prefix with a throwaway HOME and XDG dirs. Source read at the matching tag, [`sst/opencode@v1.19.4`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/tree/v1.19.4). No repo changes. ### Recommendation on separation Most of the separation isn't needed, because OpenCode already reads the two formats this repo is built from: - **Skills:** OpenCode loads `SKILL.md` natively, from `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `.opencode/skills/`, and any directory listed in `skills.paths` (scanned for `**/SKILL.md`). Unknown frontmatter such as `allowed-tools` is ignored. Pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `plugins/` found all five skills with no change. ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/), [source](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts)) - **Commands:** OpenCode's command format is the same markdown-with-frontmatter, with the same `$ARGUMENTS`. It does **not** read `.claude/commands/` or a plugin's `commands/` (only `.opencode/command(s)/`, `~/.config/opencode/command(s)/` and the `command` config key; I checked: a file in `.claude/commands/` doesn't show up). The only thing in our command files OpenCode can't use as-is is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/), [source](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/config/command.ts)) - **Claude Code plugins themselves** (`.claude-plugin/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, marketplaces, the plugin cache under `~/.claude/plugins/`) are not read at all. The `~/.claude` skill scan is anchored at `~/.claude/skills/`, so skills installed as Claude Code plugins are invisible to OpenCode. The piece that makes one tree serve both: an OpenCode server plugin's `config` hook gets the live merged config and can add to it. I prototyped a 50-line plugin (plain JS, no dependencies) that, for each `plugins/

/`, appends `plugins/

/skills` to `skills.paths`, turns each `plugins/

/commands/*.md` into an OpenCode command with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by the real path, and replaces `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` in a loaded skill's text through `tool.execute.after` on the `skill` tool. Installed by OpenCode from a git URL (`"plugin": [["name@git+file:///…", {"plugins": ["forge-tracker"]}]]`), it registered `forge-tracker` and `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom` with the script paths resolved into OpenCode's package cache, and the script ran from there with its executable bit intact. So the layout I'd propose leaves the Claude Code layout where it is and adds OpenCode code only where there's no shared form: ``` package.json # "main": "harness/opencode/index.js"; makes the repo an OpenCode plugin harness/opencode/index.js # the one OpenCode entry: registers skills + commands, resolves the two variables, # adds per-plugin extras; plugin options pick which plugins to enable plugins/

/ .claude-plugin/plugin.json # Claude Code only (unchanged) skills/

/SKILL.md, scripts/ # shared; keep ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} commands/*.md # shared; Claude Code reads them natively, the OpenCode entry registers them hooks/ # Claude Code only (hooks.json, function-hooks modules) harness/opencode/*.ts|js # only where a plugin needs OpenCode code (session-decisions; worktree-tidy's # session-start note); index.js imports these ``` Moving the Claude Code parts under `harness/claude-code/` buys nothing: Claude Code expects `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` at the plugin root and finds `commands/`, `skills/` and `hooks/` there by default, and the skills and commands are the shared format anyway. The one plugin where a real core/binding split pays off is session-decisions (below). Why one package at the repo root rather than one per plugin: OpenCode installs plugins through npm specifiers, and a git specifier can't point at a subdirectory, so `git+https://github.com/lokkju/skills.git` only works with a `package.json` at the root. Per-plugin packages would mean publishing each to npm. [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) ships exactly this shape for its many harnesses: a shared `skills/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `.codex-plugin/` and so on beside it, and a root `package.json` whose `main` is `.opencode/plugins/superpowers.js`, installed with `"plugin": ["superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git"]` ([INSTALL](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md), [plugin](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/.opencode/plugins/superpowers.js)). Its plugin registers skills through the same `config` hook. Skills-only installs keep working without the OpenCode entry: `npx skills add lokkju/skills -a opencode` (vercel-labs `skills` 1.7.4) copies the skills into `.agents/skills/`, which OpenCode reads. Tested from a local checkout. Without the entry, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` isn't filled in; OpenCode appends `Base directory for this skill:

` to the loaded skill, and our SKILL.md text already tells the model to put that directory in its place. A model that copies the command verbatim gets `/scripts/term-record: No such file or directory` (tested), so the entry's substitution is worth having. A moving target to know about: OpenCode has a **V2 plugin API** in its source tree (`define({ id, setup })`, `ctx.skill.transform`, `ctx.command.transform`; [README](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/v2/promise/README.md)), and superpowers' install notes say V2 hosts (2.0.4+) use a `plugins` key and reject a bare file path. The released npm package is still 1.19.4 with the V1 API, which is what I tested. superpowers' plugin handles both from one file; ours could do the same later. ### Per plugin | Plugin | Works in OpenCode unchanged | Needs an OpenCode equivalent | Can't port | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | forge-release | Skill and `github-app-create` (discovered; script runs from a skills-folder copy). | Nothing: no commands or hooks. | None. | | forge-tracker | Skill and `forge-tracker` script. | `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom`: registered from the same `commands/*.md` by the OpenCode entry with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolved (tested). `argument-hint` has no OpenCode field and is dropped. | None. | | term-recorder | Skill and `term-record`; tested end to end (skill loaded through OpenCode's `skill` tool, script run through `bash`). It also drives OpenCode's own TUI: I used it to snap OpenCode for this survey. | `allowed-tools`: OpenCode ignores it. Its default permission is `"*": "allow"` and skill directories are pre-allowed for `external_directory`, so it only matters for a user who sets `bash` to `ask`/`deny`. For them, the entry's `config` hook can add `"/scripts/term-record *": "allow"` (tested: the script ran while `echo` was denied by the project's `bash: {"*": "deny"}`). The rule is session-wide, not scoped to the skill being loaded. The "Claude Code as the target" section is Claude-specific; an OpenCode-target section would be new text. | None. | | worktree-tidy | Skill and `worktree-tidy report`. | The `SessionStart` note: a server plugin can run `worktree-tidy hook` on the `session.created` event and inject the note through `experimental.chat.system.transform`, or show it as a toast. Hooks exist in 1.19.4 (both are triggered in source); not tested. `allowed-tools` as for term-recorder. | None. | | session-decisions | The skill and its labelled-list fallback (#114). | Everything the mod does, written against OpenCode's APIs. `decision_*` tools: a plugin's `tool` map (custom tools tested). TaskCreate labelling: OpenCode's task list is `todowrite`, which replaces the whole list; `tool.execute.before` sees and can rewrite its args (seen, rewrite not tested). Hand-off check: the `session.idle` event fires at turn end (seen) and `experimental.text.complete` exposes the final text. Sidebar, footer, toasts, Accept: OpenCode has a TUI plugin API (`tui.json` `plugin`, a module `{ id, tui }`) with `api.slots.register` for `sidebar_content`, `session_prompt_right`, `app_bottom` and others, `api.ui.toast`, `DialogSelect`, `Prompt`, routes and keymap commands ([types](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/tui.ts)); OpenCode's own sidebar Todo list is built on it ([todo.tsx](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/sidebar/todo.tsx)). I loaded a TUI plugin and its toast showed; a sidebar section wasn't tested (it needs Solid/OpenTUI JSX). The TUI API isn't on the public plugins page. | Transcript rows (`● queued D3`, `✓ D3 · …`): there is no per-tool rendering slot. No TUI at all under `opencode run`, `serve`, ACP, web or desktop, so there the fallback list is the answer. | | session-history | The skills load. | claude-session-index reads Claude Code JSONL transcripts; OpenCode keeps sessions in SQLite (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) and has `opencode session` and `opencode export ` for JSON. Support means a new reader in [claude-session-index](https://github.com/lokkju/claude-session-index), not work in this repo. | Nothing, but nothing is useful until that reader exists. | For session-decisions my recommendation is: the fallback list is the OpenCode story now, and a second step is a server plugin with the `decision_*` tools, a store, and an idle-time hand-off toast, which works headless (and so for the cattle runner in lokkju/infra#214). The sidebar is a third step if wanted. The pure modules (`queue.ts`, `subject.ts`, `handoff.ts`, `reconcile.ts`, `lineage.ts`, `forge.ts`, `markdown.ts`, `more.ts`, about 1,300 lines) import nothing but each other and `types`, so they can move to a shared `core/` used by both `register.tsx` (Claude Code, 1,347 lines) and an OpenCode binding. That's the one plugin where a per-harness split inside the plugin is real work rather than a convention. ### Tested vs read Tested on OpenCode 1.19.4, with a scripted OpenAI-compatible mock standing in for the model (no credentials used), via `opencode debug skill`, `opencode serve` (`GET /skill`, `GET /command`), `opencode run --format json`, and the TUI under term-recorder: - `skills.paths` pointed at `plugins/` lists all five skills; `.agents/skills/` (from `npx skills add … -a opencode --copy`) and a symlink in `.claude/skills/` are found without config. - All four scripts run from a skills-folder copy (`--help`). - End to end: `skill` tool loads term-recorder, OpenCode prints the base directory, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` in a bash command expands to empty and fails, the plugin substitution fixes the text, the resolved script runs. - `.opencode/commands/*.md` is listed and shows in the `/` menu; `.claude/commands/*.md` is not. - A plugin's `config` hook adds commands, `skills.paths` entries and `permission.bash` rules, and all three take effect. - A plugin's custom tool is callable; `tool.execute.before`/`after`, `chat.message` and the `event` hook (including `session.idle`) fire. - Install from a git URL with plugin options, as described above. - A TUI plugin loads from `tui.json` and shows a toast. Read only, not tested: the TUI sidebar slots, injecting a session-start note, rewriting `todowrite` args, the V2 plugin API, and whether a plugin's `permission.ask` hook works: it's typed in [`Hooks`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/index.ts) but nothing in 1.19.4's server triggers it, so pre-approval has to go through the `config` hook. I didn't run a real model, didn't install the `git+https` form of this repo (it has no `package.json` yet), and didn't install superpowers (third-party code). Other sources: [plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), [config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/), [rules](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/) (AGENTS.md first, CLAUDE.md fallback; `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE*`), [permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [`tool/skill.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts), [`plugin/index.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts), [`agent/agent.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts) (default permissions), [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills). For step 4 (CI): the cheap smoke test needs no model. `npx skills add -a opencode -y --copy` into a temp project, run each script's `--help` from there, and assert `opencode debug skill` lists them. The mock-model run is a slightly bigger test that also proves the variable substitution and command registration. ### Open questions 1. One OpenCode package at the repo root, with plugin options to pick plugins (what I'd do, and what git install allows), or per-plugin packages published to npm? 2. Target only the V1 plugin API that ships today, or V1 and V2 from one file the way superpowers does? 3. Should the OpenCode entry add `bash` allow rules for the skills' scripts? They're session-wide, unlike `allowed-tools`, and only matter when a user has tightened `bash`. 4. session-decisions in OpenCode: fallback list only, tools plus hand-off toast, or the full sidebar? 5. Distribution and versions: install from `git+https` (pins by ref), or publish to npm, and if so whether yeet should version the OpenCode package as its own target.

An ACTION item whose subject has a top-level `(recommend ...)` clause now gets an **Accept** button beside **Done**. It answers `A<k>: go with <recommendation>`, the same wording as a DECIDE item's Accept, and those items join **Accept all**. The recommendation comes from the existing `splitBody`/`recommendation()` in `hooks/subject.ts`, so it's the item's own last top-level `(recommend ...)`, as #132 settled.

- **Cards** (inline pane and sidebar, both `drawCard`): Accept shows for any item with a recommendation. Done stays on every ACTION item; it's the primary button only when no Accept sits beside it. An ACTION item without a recommendation keeps only Done.
- **Details view** (from `[more]`, the card's label, or the transcript's `queued A1` line): the same Accept/Done pair.
- **Chip**: `recommends <choice>` already drew for any kind, so ACTION items with a recommendation show it with no change.
- **Details view top row**: at 60 columns the scroll hint squeezed the label into `A` over `1`, the chip onto two rows and the age into `0` over `m`. Those no longer shrink; the hint truncates instead. DECIDE items had the same problem before this change.
- **Skill**: an ACTION item that waits only on the user's approval for a step the agent carries out (merge, apply, tag, deploy) carries a `(recommend ...)` clause. `A2: go with <choice>` means do the step, then close the item with the result; `A2: done` means the user did it. The README describes both buttons.
- **Tests** (`tests/register.test.tsx`): an ACTION item with and without a recommendation (buttons, Done's variant, the answer text), Accept all mixing a DECIDE with two ACTION items (one without a recommendation, which it skips), Accept all showing for two recommended actions alone, and the details view's buttons and Accept answer.

I checked it on screen with term-recorder on Claude Code 2.1.317, using `/decisions pane` with one recommended action, one plain action and one decision. At 100x30, 60x30 and 40x30 the card row reads `[ Accept ] [ Done ] [ Answer ]` with the link on the right. In the details view, `[ Accept ] [ Done ] [ Answer ] [ Back ]` sits on one row at 60 and wraps `[ Back ]` to a second row at 40.

Closes #145

Claude Code hard-wraps a long code-block line at the pane width, and copying it out of tmux turns each wrap into a line break, so a long one-liner handed to the operator runs in pieces.

**Skill.** Under actions: when the step is a command, write it to a script (the session's scratch directory, or a task in the repo's task runner) and hand over one short line that runs it; otherwise keep every line well under 80 columns, split with `\` continuations, never one long line. The same applies to items: the subject is one line, so it points at the script or keeps the command short, and anything longer goes in the description, split the same way.

**Check.** The hand-off check (classic.Stop, and turn.complete when Stop is passed over) now also looks at code blocks for a line over 100 columns that is a shell command: any line of a `bash`/`sh`/`console`/other shell block, or a line of an unlabelled block that reads as a command (a `$` prompt, `sudo`, an `&&`/`||` chain, a word followed by flags). Language-tagged non-shell blocks, prose, and log-like lines in unlabelled blocks are left alone. It shows a toast (`A 110-column command line: copied from tmux it breaks at the wrap`) and, from classic.Stop, reminds the model with the next prompt to hand it over again as a script or split lines. It rides on the existing `handoff_check` option, whose description now says so.

Checked in a real Claude Code session with term-recorder at 100x30 and 60x30 (Haiku replying with the 110-column `systemctl` one-liner from the issue): the toast draws whole in its box at both widths, and at 60 columns the reply shows the hard wrap the issue describes.

Closes #137
response.title: fix(session-decisions): hand over commands as a script or short lines

response.body:
Long shell commands that Claude Code hands to the operator break when copied out of a tmux pane: the terminal UI wraps each line at the pane width, and tmux copy-mode (and most terminal selection inside tmux) copies those soft wraps as hard line breaks. Pasted into a shell, the command runs in pieces or fails.

Seen 2026-10-26 in an infra session over ssh + tmux 3.4 in Rio: a `sudo systemctl ... && sudo rm ... && sudo systemctl daemon-reload ...` one-liner handed over for the operator to run.

## What the skills could do

Whatever hands commands to the operator (session-decisions' action items, and any skill or instruction that prints "run this"):

1. **Prefer a script file over a long command.** Write the steps to a file (under the session's scratch dir or the repo's task runner, e.g. a mise task) and give one short line to run it: `bash ~/.claude/jobs/<id>/tmp/remove-heartbeat.sh`. Short lines survive any wrap.
2. **Otherwise keep every line short** (well under 80 columns), so no line is ever wrapped. `&&` chains and `\` continuations are fine and copy cleanly; only a line wider than the pane breaks. Split a long command across lines with `\` rather than leaving one long line.

## Upstream

The root cause is that Claude Code's renderer hard-wraps long lines in code blocks instead of letting the terminal soft-wrap them (which tmux would then copy as one line), or offering a copy action for a code block. Worth reporting to Claude Code as well; tracked here so the skills work around it in the meantime.
response.title: Commands handed to the operator break when copied from tmux (wrapped lines become line breaks)

The hand-off check's unknown-label rule flagged `D123` quoted from [#129](https://github.com/lokkju/skills/issues/129) as an item this session never created, and the nudge told the model to create it.

A label now counts as the session's own only when:

- its bullet (or, in other lines, its sentence) holds no issue or PR reference and no link;
- that sentence doesn't say where it quotes from (`from the issue`, `in that PR`, `the other session`);
- it is no more than 50 above the session's highest label of its letter (D123 against a queue at D52 reads as foreign).

A label leading its line (`D7: merge it`) is always the session's, so the usual item shape still gets caught beside a reference. A line whose only labels are foreign is treated as unlabelled: it is still flagged if it hands a step over (`You'll need to merge #12 (A7).` still flags, as a hand-off rather than as a missing label).

The nudge now says to create the item only if it is one of this session's, and to ignore a label quoted from an issue, a PR, a document or another session.

Tests cover both lines from the real case, the range rule, and that `D7: merge X` with D7 unqueued still flags. The README's list of what the check skips has the new rule.

Closes #131

response.body:
`/groom` finds merged-but-open issues only when a merge commit or PR body carries a closing
reference (`Closes #N`). In a repo where work lands without them, that whole class is invisible,
and those issues accumulate silently — which is the failure mode `/groom` exists to catch.

## What happened

On a private repo with 47 open issues, `/groom` proposed 6 fixes: 2 `link-add`, 4
`delete-branch`. It proposed **zero** closes.

Five of those open issues were in fact complete, delivered across two large merged PRs. Neither
merge commit used a closing keyword, so `/groom` could not see any of them. A human spotted all
five by reading the issue titles against what had shipped, and closed them by hand.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than just writing better commit messages

The closing-reference convention fails in exactly the repos that need grooming most: ones where
work lands in large PRs, where one issue is satisfied by several commits across several PRs, or
where the PR predates the issue. `/groom` already reads merged PRs since a date — it has the
titles and the changed paths in hand.

It is also the one proposal class where being wrong is cheap: a wrongly-closed issue is
reopened in one click, unlike a deleted branch or a written link.

## Possible shapes, least invasive first

1. **A "possibly done" section, listed rather than proposed** — same status as the existing
   *Listed for you* items. Name the issue, the merged PR that looks like it, and the signal
   (title overlap, or the issue naming a path that PR changed). No write, no approval, no risk.
   This alone would have surfaced all five.
2. **A proposal class gated on stronger evidence** — the issue's body names a path or symbol a
   merged PR changed, *and* the issue has had no activity since that merge. Proposed by number
   like any other fix.
3. **Ask the forge.** GitHub's timeline API records `cross-referenced` events when a PR mentions
   an issue in any form, not only with closing keywords. Cheaper than diffing, and already on
   the wire.

## What I would not do

Don't infer closure from label or milestone state, and don't close on title similarity alone.
Both would produce confident wrong closes in a repo with near-duplicate issues, which is the
other thing `/groom` is meant to find.

## A smaller, related observation from the same run

The report's *Skipped (not configured)* section correctly named three checks that need
`.claude/forge-tracker.local.md`. That part works and the message is clear.

But the combination — no label config *and* no closing references — meant `/groom` had almost
nothing to work with, and nothing in the output said so. The report reads the same whether it
ran every check and found little, or ran two checks out of six. A line stating which checks
actually ran, rather than only which were skipped, would set expectations honestly and would
have prompted a closer look sooner.
response.title: forge-tracker /groom cannot see merged-but-open issues without a closing reference

response.body:
In the session-decisions panel, a DECIDE item with a recommendation gets an **Accept** button, which answers `D<k>: go with <recommendation>`, and it counts toward **Accept all**. An ACTION item gets only **Done**, even when its subject carries a recommendation.

In practice many ACTION items are approvals the agent can carry out once the user says go, and they come with a recommendation:

```
A12 ACTION: approve merging owner/repo#34 (CI green) (recommend merge) [owner/repo#34]
A13 ACTION: approve merging owner/repo#56 and tagging v1.2.0 (recommend merge and tag) [owner/repo#56]
```

For these, **Done** is the wrong word: the user hasn't done anything. They want to approve the step so the agent does it. Today they have to type `A12: go` by hand.

## Proposal

- When an ACTION item's body has a `(recommend ...)` clause, show an **Accept** button beside **Done**. It answers `A<k>: go with <recommendation>`, matching the DECIDE wording, so the agent gets the same signal either way.
- Include those ACTION items in **Accept all** (in `register.tsx`, the `accepts` list now reads the recommendation only for `item.kind === 'DECIDE'`).
- Show the `recommends <choice>` chip on ACTION items that have one, as DECIDE items do.
- Keep **Done** for ACTION items, recommendation or not, for the case where the user really did the step themselves.
- An ACTION item without a recommendation keeps only **Done**.

## Notes

- `recommendation()` and `shortRecommendation()` in `hooks/subject.ts` already parse the clause; the change is which kinds the panel applies them to.
- The skill text (SKILL.md) can say ACTION items that need the user's approval should carry a `(recommend ...)` clause, so they get the button.
- Tests: `tests/register.test.tsx` covering an ACTION item with and without a recommendation, and Accept all mixing both kinds.
response.title: session-decisions: an Accept button for ACTION items that carry a recommendation

The GitLab half of the read-only forge layer from #21. `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom` and `smoke` now run on GitLab, self-hosted included, with no change to the reports beyond writing merge requests as `!N`.

## What it does

- **Transport.** Every GitLab read is `glab api --hostname <host> --include --method GET <endpoint>`, so glab's login, host settings (`api_host`) and pinned `ca_cert` apply and no GitLab token passes through forge-tracker. The output is parsed for status, `Link`, `X-Next-Page` and body, so pagination, the page cap and the named HTTP errors work as on GitHub. The glab transport refuses anything but a GET as well, below `check_read`. glab's stderr is redacted, with the GitLab token prefixes (`glpat-`, `gloas-`, `glrt-` and the rest) and `PRIVATE-TOKEN:` added to the patterns.
- **Adapter** (`forges/gitlab.py`): every read the GitHub adapter answers, in the same normalized shapes. Identity with `bot`; issues open and updated since; comments since from the project's note events; mentions from your pending to-do items; open MRs with a per-MR read for head pipeline, settled `detailed_merge_status` and approvals; merged MRs with `closes_issues`; newest default-branch pipeline by `source` with failed jobs; jobs that passed only on retry (`include_retried`, newest attempt by id); branches with `compare`; tags and releases; milestones, label events, notes, `commits/:sha/refs`, issue refs, links and `closed_by` for `/groom` and `/next`; the `/next` fingerprint.
- **Mergeability** is three-valued from `detailed_merge_status`: `unchecked`, `checking`, `preparing`, `approvals_syncing` or a missing status is `unknown` even when `has_conflicts` says false.
- **Blocking.** Native `is_blocked_by` links count; with `blocking: relates_to+blocked` (GitLab CE), a `relates_to` link from an issue carrying the blocked label counts too, marked `convention`. Any other `blocking:` value is refused.
- **Self-hosted.** `api_base:` names an API under a subpath; a URL under `https://<host>/api/v4` goes to glab as a path so glab's own base applies.
- **Detection.** `gitlab.com`, or any host in glab's `config.yml` (`hosts:` keys and `api_host`, read without running glab, tokens never read), or `GITLAB_HOST`, is GitLab.
- **Reports.** Merge requests are `!N` in catchup, next (facts, slate validation) and groom, and the text says MR where it said PR. Writes aren't built for GitLab: `groom apply`, `write` and `link` refuse with that reason unless a `write_wrapper:` is set, and `/groom` prints a `writes: unsupported on GitLab` line.

## Tests

- `tests/test_contract.py` is the shared contract suite: bot flag, issue fields, three-valued mergeability (including GitLab's `unchecked` with `has_conflicts: false`), change fields, merged-since window and closing issues, native links, a read failing on its own, a page cap as a failed read, a token in an error as `***`, failed jobs, tags, reference form. Each scenario is written once; `tests/kits.py` has a kit per forge that puts it in that forge's response shapes. Three GitHub tests it now covers were dropped from `test_github.py`.
- `tests/test_gitlab.py`: the glab transport through a fake `run`, every GitLab-specific read, and the four reports over `tests/fixtures/gitlab/world.json` (a small project in GitLab's documented REST shapes, served under a subpath `api_base`) against golden output.

## Live runs

No GitLab login exists on this machine (glab wasn't installed, so I installed it through mise only to exercise the transport, and it has no login), so there's no authenticated smoke run and no recorded fixtures. To check the transport and the response shapes, I ran the adapter unauthenticated and read-only against a public gitlab.com project: repo, open issues, issues since, comments since, open MRs with detail, merged MRs with closing issues, push and schedule pipelines, retried jobs, branches with compare, tags, closing refs and issue refs all read correctly. `/user`, labels, milestones, notes, label events and links need a login there and returned 401, so those are covered only by fixtures. Nothing was written to any forge.

Checks: `uvx ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the plugin, the pytest suite (563 passed) and `claude plugin validate --strict` on the plugin and the marketplace.

Refs #21

The Forgejo (and Gitea) half of the read-only forge layer from #21, which finishes it. Stacked on [#141](https://github.com/lokkju/skills/pull/141) (GitLab): the diff against that branch is this PR's work, and it goes to `main` once #141 merges.

## What it does

- **Transport.** urllib against `/api/v1`, with `Authorization: token <t>` and lists paged by `limit=50` (Forgejo's default maximum), following `Link`. The token is `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, else the token of tea's login for the host, read from tea's `config.yml`; tea itself isn't run, since its output is meant for terminals and covers only part of these reads (the spec's ruling). The API base is `api_base:`, else the tea login's URL plus `/api/v1` (so an instance under a subpath needs only its tea login), else `https://<host>/api/v1`; `ca_file:` pins the CA. The token is a redaction secret like GitHub's.
- **Adapter** (`forges/forgejo.py`): every read the other two answer, in the same shapes. Issues, comments, mentions (issue search, `mentioned=true`, kept to this repo), open PRs with a per-PR combined commit status and reviews, merged PRs (read back by `recentupdate` until one predates the window), native blocking from issue dependencies, branches and reachability through `compare`, tags and releases, milestones, label history from the issue timeline, issue refs, and the `/next` fingerprint.
- **Closing references** aren't an API on Forgejo, so they come from closing keywords in PR bodies (`Closes #4`, `fixes acme/widgets#5`, `Resolves #6, #7`; code spans and blocks don't count), in a new `refs.closing_numbers`.
- **CI.** Both runs API shapes are read (Gitea's GitHub-shaped one and Forgejo's own). On an instance without one (a 404 while the repo itself reads), the push run falls back to the default branch head's combined commit status, and the scheduled run and the retried jobs are **unsupported**.
- **Unsupported, not empty.** New `model.Unsupported`; `attempt` marks the `Read` `unsupported` (still not `ok`, so nothing takes it for data). `/catchup` prints `<part>: unsupported on Forgejo (<reason>)` in Health, lists it under `health.unsupported` in `--json`, and doesn't count it as a failure, so the marker still moves; `smoke` prints it the same way. Everywhere else an unsupported read stays a FAILED part.
- **Detection.** A host with a tea login is Forgejo; otherwise an unauthenticated `GET https://<host>/api/v1/version` with a JSON `version` means Forgejo or Gitea, cached per host for a day in `hosts.json` (a host that gave no HTTP answer isn't cached). A remote under a subpath is read as `owner/repo`.
- **Mergeability.** `mergeable: true` is no conflict, `false` a conflict, anything else unknown. The API has no "still checking" state, so `false` right after a base moves can't be told apart; I couldn't measure that against a live instance.
- Writes stay GitHub only, refused on Forgejo without a `write_wrapper:` (as on GitLab).

Fixes found by the live run below: Forgejo answers an empty list as JSON `null`, answers a repo with releases turned off with a 404, and writes times in the server's own offset; all three are handled and tested.

## Tests

- The contract suite now runs over all three forges (`ForgejoKit` in `tests/kits.py`): 45 cases.
- `tests/test_forgejo.py`: auth scheme and paging, closing keywords, per-PR status and reviews, merged-since stop, closing refs, dependencies, timeline label events, mentions, both runs shapes, the commit-status fallback and the unsupported reads, a runs 404 on a missing repo staying a failure, null lists, disabled releases, compare, the token and subpath API base from a tea login, the probe and its cache, and the four reports over `tests/fixtures/forgejo/world.json` (a repo in Forgejo's documented shapes, on an instance with no runs API) against golden output.
- Detection tests for tea logins (both YAML list indents) and the probe order.

## Live runs

No tea login or FORGEJO_TOKEN exists on this machine (tea isn't installed), so there's no authenticated smoke run and no recorded fixtures. I ran the adapter unauthenticated and read-only against a public Codeberg repo: the version probe found Forgejo; repo, open issues, issues since, comments since, open PRs with status and reviews, merged PRs, labels, milestones, tags, dependencies, closing refs from PR bodies, branches with compare, the fingerprint, timeline label events, issue refs and reachability all read correctly, and Codeberg has no Actions runs API, so the push run came from the commit status and the scheduled run and retried jobs showed as unsupported. `/user` needs a token (401). Nothing was written to any forge.

response.body:
Part of #12 (forge-tracker). A read-only forge layer that the briefing and grooming commands use. It is filed as its own piece, because the three commands built on it each need the same reads on all three forges.

**The forges.** GitHub (`gh`, REST plus GraphQL where REST is thin), GitLab (`glab api`, including self-hosted with a subpath and a pinned CA) and Forgejo/Gitea (`tea` where it covers the read, otherwise the REST API with the user's token). Each forge is detected from the repo's remote, the same way #12 already plans.

**What every adapter answers, in one normalized shape:**
- **Identity:** the authenticated user, and whether an account is a bot.
- **Issues:** open issues, and issues updated since a time. Each carries labels, milestone (title, due date), assignees, created/updated/closed timestamps and comments since a time.
- **Links between issues:** native blocking where the forge has it (GitHub "blocked by" issue dependencies and sub-issues, Forgejo dependencies, GitLab `blocks` on tiers that have it). Where it doesn't (GitLab CE has only `relates_to`), a configurable convention such as `relates_to` plus a `blocked` label.
- **PRs/MRs:** open, and merged since a time. Each carries title, source branch, merge commit sha, reviewers/assignees, draft and conflict state, and head pipeline status.
- **CI:** the newest pipeline/workflow run on the default branch by trigger (push vs schedule), its failed jobs, and jobs that passed only on retry.
- **Branches:** remote branch heads, and which have no open PR/MR.
- **Tags/releases:** the newest tags and releases. Container registry tags are optional, and only where configured.

**Rules learned building this once:**
- **GET only, enforced at the boundary.** The adapter's transport refuses any method but GET, so a read-only command can't write even by mistake.
- **Paginate to the end, or fail loudly.** A page cap that is hit is a FAILED read, never a silently short list that renders as "none".
- **Every read can fail on its own.** It returns data or a named error, and callers print `<part>: FAILED (<reason>)`, never an empty section.
- **The shared account.** Agents usually authenticate as the user, so nothing may treat "the user's account did X" as "the user did X", and no assignee is a signal that a human must act.
- **No secrets in errors.** Error text includes the CLI's stderr truncated, never tokens.
- **Injectable fetch.** Tests feed canned payloads per forge, with no network.

**Done when:** each forge's adapter passes the same contract test suite over recorded fixtures, plus one live read-only smoke run per forge.
response.title: forge-tracker: a read-only forge layer for GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo

Step 2 of #126: the repo is now an OpenCode plugin, built the way the [survey](https://github.com/lokkju/skills/issues/126#issuecomment-6415744883) proposed and you approved. ## What's here - `package.json` at the root (`@lokkju/skills`) with `harness/opencode/index.js` as its entry, plain ESM JavaScript, no dependencies. OpenCode 1.19.4 runs it as a V1 plugin module (`export default { id, server }`); `engines.opencode` is `>=1.19.4 <2`, since 1.19.4 is the only version I tested and V2 is a different API. - The `config` hook appends each enabled `plugins/

/skills` to `skills.paths` and registers each `plugins/

/commands/*.md` as an OpenCode command, with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolved and `description` carried over (`argument-hint` has no OpenCode field and is dropped). A command the user already defines under the same name is left alone. - `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` is filled in three places: the `skill` tool's output (`tool.execute.after`), a file `read` from inside one of our skill directories (forge-release's `references/yeet-setup.md` uses it), and OpenCode's `/` commands. That last one the survey didn't mention: OpenCode turns every skill into a slash command whose template is the raw SKILL.md, so `/worktree-tidy` got the unresolved variable until `command.execute.before` handled it. - Options: `plugins` (list of names; all when unset; an unknown name fails the load, so a typo can't quietly turn one off) and `allowScripts` (default off), which adds `bash` allow rules for each executable in `skills/*/scripts/`, both bare and quoted, since OpenCode matches the command text as written and our skills quote the path. They're appended after the user's own rules, so they win for those scripts; that's in the README. - No per-plugin `plugins/

/harness/opencode/`: nothing needs one yet. - `files` ships the entry plus `plugins/*/skills/**` and `plugins/*/commands/**` (63 files, 156 kB packed); no tests, hooks, `.claude-plugin/` or docs. `license` is `PolyForm-Shield-1.0.0` (an SPDX id), plus `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`. - README: an OpenCode install section (`git+https` now, the npm name once published, the options, and what doesn't carry over). AGENTS.md: a `harness/` section and the new CI job. - CI: an `opencode` job runs `npm test` (Node's built-in runner, 14 tests: fake config, `skills.paths`, commands and path substitution, options, both substitution hooks) and checks `npm pack --dry-run` ships the entry and commands and none of the Claude Code-only files. `claude plugin validate --strict .` still passes with the root `package.json`. ## Plugins in OpenCode - forge-release, forge-tracker, term-recorder, worktree-tidy: skills and scripts work; forge-tracker's `/catchup`, `/next` and `/groom` are registered. - session-decisions: skill only, which falls back to the labelled list in the reply (no TaskCreate or `decision_*` tools there). It has no `commands/`, and `/decisions` comes from its function-hooks module, so there was nothing to exclude. - Out of scope: session-history (reads Claude Code transcripts; lives in lokkju/claude-session-index), every `hooks/hooks.json` and function-hooks module, and `allowed-tools`. - Follow-up: worktree-tidy's session-start note. It isn't trivial in V1: the hook's text points at `/worktree-tidy` and Claude Code's session directories, it needs a `session.created` handler plus `experimental.chat.system.transform`, and the survey left that path untested. ## Tested With OpenCode 1.19.4 from npm in a scratch prefix (throwaway HOME and XDG dirs, a scripted OpenAI-compatible mock as the model, no credentials): - Installed from `git+file` of this branch and from `git+https://github.com/lokkju/skills.git#feat/opencode-harness`. - `opencode debug skill` lists all five skills from the installed package; `opencode serve` `GET /command` lists `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom` with the script path resolved into OpenCode's package cache, and `GET /config` shows the `allowScripts` rules. - `opencode run --command next` and `--command catchup` (both install forms): the mock found the resolved, quoted script path in the prompt, called `bash` with it, and `forge-tracker --help` ran while the project's `permission.bash` was `{"*": "deny"}`. - `--command worktree-tidy` (a skill as a command) and the `skill` tool loading term-recorder: no `${CLAUDE_` left in what the model saw, and the resolved script ran. - With `{"plugins": ["forge-tracker"]}` and no `allowScripts`: only that skill listed, and OpenCode withheld `bash` entirely under the deny rule. ## Not done: npm and yeet Nothing is published. `@lokkju/skills`, `@lokkju/opencode-skills`, `lokkju-skills` and `opencode-lokkju-skills` are all unregistered on npm, and the `@lokkju` scope belongs to the npm account `lokkju`. response.body:
`/catchup` and `/next` run against the repo at the session's working directory, which isn't always the project the session is about. In a session launched from `~/projects/infra` that spent its whole length building `codexpublicus/captare`, "catchup and next" meant captare. The commands read lokkju/infra instead: catchup moved infra's marker (so the operator's own next infra catchup skips that window), and `/next` produced a 43-issue slate and three queued decisions for the wrong repo.

The skills should work out which project or projects the session is about before running the CLI:

- Look at what the session has been doing: repos it committed to, pushed, opened PRs or issues on, or explicitly named. Treat the working directory as one candidate among those, not the default.
- One clear candidate that isn't the working directory: say which repo you're about to read and run with `--repo <dir>`.
- Several candidates (a session that touched infra and captare, say): ask which ones, offering the session's repos plus "all of them", and for `/catchup` run a workspace-style report across the chosen ones.
- The working directory is the only candidate: run as today.

The ask belongs before the first read, because `/catchup` moves its marker. A wrong guess costs the operator a window of their own catchup, not just a wasted report. When an agent runs either command for its own orientation (the `--no-mark` case), the same choice applies, but it can settle it without asking.

response.body:
A ruling that stops holding after its item is closed now has a recorded path instead of prose.

## What it does

- **`decision_supersede`** (new tool: `label`, `by`, `why`) marks a settled item, task-list or ledger, with `Superseded (<date>) by D<m>: <why>`. The item stays completed; the line is what shows it superseded. It refuses an open item (those already settle as `Ruling: superseded by D<m>` through TaskUpdate or `decision_close`), an unknown label, and a `by` that isn't another item in the queue, so the new item has to exist first.
- **Superseded, not just completed:** `/decisions all` tags the old item `(superseded)` and prints its Superseded line under the ruling. In the sidebar's Settled list and the transcript line it draws as `→ D1 2026-10-26 · superseded by D2: <why>` (`>` under NO_COLOR) where a completed item draws `✓`.
- **The new item says what it replaces:** its card gets a dim `replaces D1: <old ruling>` line, the details view a `Replaces D1: ..., whose ruling no longer holds.` paragraph, `/decisions all` a `replaces` line, and its reconcile-brief row ends `(supersedes D1: <old ruling>)`. The brief lists open items only, so the old item shows there through the new item's row. With no ruling recorded, the old question stands in.
- **Skill:** "When an open item changes" covers a closed item that proves unworkable: create the new item, call `decision_supersede` without trying TaskUpdate first, and say so in the reply. "When the user answers" points there. The README's Answering and sync sections describe it.

## Choices

- **The link lives on the old item.** `supersedes` isn't a separate field on the new item. One call writes the Superseded line on the old item, and the new item's "replaces" is derived by finding the item whose line names it. TaskCreate has no field the plugin could use, and putting it in the subject would fight the one-line subject. One record means the two sides can't disagree. The skill also asks for a "Supersedes D1" note in the new item's description, but nothing reads it.
- **Why TaskUpdate said `Task not found`:** Claude Code deletes a list's task files once every task in it is completed (the `.highwatermark` keeps ids from being reused). The plugin's stored record only kept task items that `decision_close` had settled, so after a compaction or resume a completed item whose file was gone dropped out of the queue entirely. Its `closed` map now keeps a copy of every settled task-list item: completed through TaskUpdate, settled by `decision_close`, or marked by `decision_supersede`. `mergeHydrated` already restored `closed` items whose files are gone; it now also carries the Superseded line onto an item whose file is still there. A TaskUpdate that reopens or deletes the task drops the copy, as before. A later TaskUpdate whose description leaves out the recorded ruling or Superseded line keeps them.
- **The store, not TaskUpdate.** `decision_supersede` writes only to the queue's record, even when the task file still exists, so there's one path whether or not TaskUpdate can reach the task. The task file's description doesn't get the line, so ctrl+t won't show it. `/decisions`, the sidebar and the brief do.

## Checked

`claude plugin test plugins/session-decisions` passes (142 tests), with new ones for `supersede`/`replaces`/`supersededIn`, the listing, `mergeHydrated` with the file present and gone, the brief row, and two pane tests. One covers the issue's sequence: complete D1, its task file deleted, TaskUpdate answering `Task not found`, `decision_supersede` D1 by D2, then a resume that re-reads the files and still shows D1 superseded. The other is the ledger equivalent. I ran it on Claude Code 2.1.306 with the term-recorder skill, a Haiku session doing the real TaskCreate, TaskUpdate and `decision_supersede` calls. At 100x30 the transcript shows `→ D1 2026-10-26 · superseded by D2: the web JSON is blocked for every server-side request`, `/decisions all` shows the tags and lines above, and the D2 card reads `replaces D1: try the web JSON for now` under its question. At 60x30 the card and the listing wrap cleanly inside the frame.

Closes #125

response.body:
session-decisions covers superseding an item that is still open ("If the answer turns it into a different question, don't reuse the label: complete the old item with `Ruling (<date>): superseded by D<m>`"). It has no path for an item that's already closed when its ruling stops holding.

## What happened (2026-10-25, a nopantsvintage session)

- D2 asked how to read Depop listings. The user ruled "try the web JSON for now", and I completed D2 with that ruling.
- A research spike then found the web JSON blocked for every server-side request, so the ruling couldn't be carried out. I opened D5 with the new question.
- To mark D2 as superseded, I ran TaskUpdate on its task id to append `Ruling (<date>): superseded by D5`. It returned `Task not found`. The completed task was no longer reachable, so D2's record still shows a ruling that no longer holds, with no pointer to D5.

## Wanted

- **A way to supersede a closed item:** append a `Superseded (<date>) by D<m>: <why>` line to its record, and show it as superseded, not just completed, in `/decisions` and the sidebar. This is for when the ruling's premise fails, not when the user changes their mind about an open item.
- **A `supersedes` field on the new item** (D5 supersedes D2), so the new card can show "replaces D2: <old ruling>" and the user sees what changed without searching.
- **A fallback for the task list:** when TaskUpdate can't reach a completed task, the skill should send this through the ledger (`decision_update` or a new `decision_supersede`), which keeps closed items, instead of the agent writing it only in prose.
- **Skill text:** a line in "When an open item changes" or "When the user answers" covering a closed ruling that turns out unworkable: open the new item with `supersedes`, mark the old one, and say so in the reply.

response.body:
Accepting a DECIDE item now answers with the item's own recommendation: the last `(recommend ...)` that sits outside any other parentheses, before the link token. Its closing parenthesis is still found by depth, so nested parentheses inside the choice survive (`(recommend B (cheaper, (mostly)), then A)` comes back whole).

Every reader of the recommendation already went through one function, `findRecommendation` in `hooks/subject.ts`, so the fix is there and nowhere else disagrees:

- Accept on a card and in the details view, and the reconcile brief, read it through `splitBody`.
- Accept all read it through `recommendation()`, which now just returns `splitBody(body).recommendation` instead of parsing on its own.
- `problems()` (the TaskCreate and `decision_add` check) uses the same finder on the body without its link token. `parseDraft` and `formatSubject` don't parse the recommendation; they pass the body through untouched.

A `(recommend ...)` inside another parenthesis, such as `(A, the fast one (recommend for demos))`, is treated as an option note and skipped. If parentheses elsewhere in the subject never balance and nothing is left at the top level, it falls back to the last `(recommend ...)` at any depth, so a stray `(` in the question can't hide the recommendation.

I didn't add a stored recommendation field. The subject is what the task list keeps and what the hook re-reads on hydrate; a second field would need a home in the task description or the ledger and would drift from the subject whenever the agent revises it with TaskUpdate. Taking the last top-level one fixes the D123 shape without that.

The skill's "Creating an item" section gains one sentence saying the last `(recommend ...)` before the link is the one Accept uses.

Tests: the issue's D123 shape (`recommendation`, `splitBody` and `problems`), nested parentheses in the item's own recommendation, a recommendation nested inside an option's parenthesis, unbalanced parentheses elsewhere, and a pane test that presses Accept and Accept all on a two-recommendation item.

Closes #129
response.title: fix(session-decisions): accept the item's own recommendation, not an option note's

response.body:
Accepting a DECIDE item can submit the wrong recommendation when the item's text contains more than one `(recommend ...)` phrase. The answer that comes back is built from the first `(recommend ...)` in the subject, even when that one sits inside an option's description, rather than from the item's own recommendation at the end.

## What happened

A DECIDE item with several sub-decisions described one option in place, with a nested recommendation, and ended with the item's overall recommendation:

```
D123 DECIDE: ... P2 a docket profile (27,932 keyed): two-digit years (agent) or four-digit
(recommend four: every docket since 2006 and most records print four digits); P3 ...;
P4 ... (recommend all, P2 with four-digit years, P4 with a follow-up to re-key those) [...]
```

Accepting it produced:

```
D123: go with four: every docket since 2006 and most records print four digits
```

That's the nested option note, not the item's recommendation. The user had to append the real one by hand, with a question mark, to be sure it was applied.

Items with a single trailing `(recommend ...)` come back intact, including long ones with numbered parts, e.g. `go with (1) ...; (2) ...; (3) ...`.

## Expected

Accept uses the item's own recommendation: the last `(recommend ...)` in the subject (the one just before the link token), or better, a recommendation stored as a separate field when the item is created, so nested parentheses in the description can't be mistaken for it.

## Possible fixes

- Take the last `(recommend ...)` rather than the first, matching parentheses properly.
- Have `TaskCreate`/`decision_add` reject DECIDE subjects with more than one `(recommend ...)`, so authors write option notes another way (e.g. "four-digit, suggested because ...").
- Store the recommendation separately from the subject, so the subject can say anything.
response.title: session-decisions: accepting an item uses the first (recommend ...) in its text, not the item's own recommendation

response.body:
The plugins here are written for Claude Code. #118 (merged as #123) made the skills' scripts portable: each script now lives in its skill's own directory and SKILL.md calls it through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, so a skill installed by `npx skills add`, OpenCode's `skills` config or a plain skills folder can run it. That fixes the paths, nothing more. This issue is the rest: port what can be ported to other harnesses, starting with OpenCode, and give the plugins that need it a per-harness layer.

**What each plugin depends on today:**
- **forge-release, forge-tracker, worktree-tidy, term-recorder:** a skill plus standard-library Python. These should mostly work anywhere once the paths are right. Claude Code-only pieces:
  - the slash commands (`commands/*.md`);
  - worktree-tidy's session-start hook (`hooks/hooks.json`);
  - term-recorder's `allowed-tools` pre-approval;
  - forge-tracker's catchup/next/groom commands.
- **session-decisions:** a Claude Code function-hooks mod (pane, TaskCreate labelling, hand-off checks, `decision_*` tools) plus a skill. Only the skill and its no-plugin fallback (#114) work elsewhere.
- **session-history:** wraps the claude-session-index CLI, which reads Claude Code transcripts.

**To decide and build:**
1. **Survey:** for each plugin, list what works unchanged in OpenCode, what needs a per-harness equivalent (commands, hooks, tool pre-approval, MCP tools, a UI surface) and what can't port. Test with a real OpenCode install, not from docs alone.
2. **Layout for per-harness parts:** for example `plugins/<name>/harness/<harness>/` next to the shared skill and scripts, with the shared skill text written harness-neutral and each harness's extras (OpenCode plugin/commands, Claude Code hooks/commands) kept beside it. Record the convention in AGENTS.md, as was done for the minimum Claude Code version.
3. **OpenCode first:** port the skill-plus-script plugins and their commands. For session-decisions, decide whether an OpenCode plugin (its plugin API, a TUI or tool surface) can carry the queue, or whether the skill's labelled-list fallback is the OpenCode story.
4. **CI:** at least a smoke test that each portable skill's script runs from a skills-folder install, not only from the Claude Code plugin cache.
5. **Install docs** per harness in each README and the top-level README.

Related: #118 and #123 (paths), #114 (session-decisions' no-plugin fallback), #124 (minimum Claude Code version), lokkju/infra#214 (headless agents for the cattle runner, which may pick OpenCode).

response.body:
## Findings

`cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin` is a security plugin built into Claude Code. It seats itself outermost on a machine with managed settings and for Team and Enterprise organizations, and its `register` sends `classic.*`, `prompt.section/context/attachment/compose`, `skill.prompt`, `attribution.text`, `session.compact`, `settings.read` and the `session.append` attachment, hook-context and compaction doors on past every person-installed plugin (`next.to(e, "append")`). That is the "runs first and sent the event on past it" notice in the issue. It doesn't touch `tool.call`, `session.start`, `turn.*` or `ui.*`.

What session-decisions loses there: `classic.SessionStart` (the open-items reminder after compaction or resume), `classic.UserPromptSubmit` (delivers the hand-off reminder to the model) and `classic.Stop` (the hand-off check and its toast). What still works: TaskCreate labelling and the subject checks (`tool.call`), `decision_add` and the other tools, the cards, the sidebar, the footer and `/decisions`.

The seat is legitimate, so this routes nothing around it: no context goes to the model through another door.

## Changes

- **Toast at turn end.** `turn.complete` exists (2.1.306 types: `answer`, `reason`, `agentId`) and isn't in the guard's list. When `classic.Stop` didn't run for a main-loop turn, the check runs there on `e.answer` and raises the same toast. `classic.Stop` sets a flag that `turn.complete` clears, so a turn is checked once. `turn.complete` only toasts; the model-facing reminder stays on `classic.Stop` and `classic.UserPromptSubmit`. It skips subagent turns and turns that ended other than with an answer.
- **Skill.** When the assistant sees the skipped-hook notice naming session-decisions and cc-plugin-sec-default, it tells the user once what's off, queues every hand-off itself without waiting for a check, and calls `decision_list` (or TaskList) after a compaction.
- **README.** The requirements section names the guard, what goes and what still works.

## Checked

- `claude plugin test plugins/session-decisions`: 138 pass, three new tests for the `turn.complete` path (Stop passed over toasts without a model reminder; a turn whose Stop ran isn't checked twice; subagent, interrupted and queued replies pass quietly).
- `claude plugin validate --strict plugins/session-decisions` and `tsc` against the 2.1.306 types pass.
- On screen with term-recorder (Claude Code 2.1.306, `--plugin-dir`, haiku): with a temporary debug toast, `classic.Stop` runs before `turn.complete` (`stopRan=true`, one hand-off toast). With `classic.Stop` short-circuited to stand in for the guard, `turn.complete` raised the hand-off toast. I couldn't seat the real guard, which needs managed settings.

One gap left: under the guard `turnStarted` is never set (it comes from `classic.UserPromptSubmit`), so the turn-end check counts every settled item as covering its line, not just this turn's. That can only hide a toast, never raise a wrong one.

Closes #120

## What happened

In a Claude Code background session (2.1.289) with the session-decisions plugin loaded (cache version 2026.10.20.2 at session start; 2026.10.23.1 is also in the cache), the harness reported three of the plugin's classic hooks as skipped, each with the same reason:

```
session-decisions: its classic.SessionStart hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.
session-decisions: its classic.UserPromptSubmit hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.
session-decisions: its classic.Stop hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.
```

The first two arrived right after `/reload-plugins` (run three times in a row); the Stop one arrived at the end of the next turn. Earlier in the same session, before the reloads, the hooks ran: `TaskCreate` with a `DECIDE: ... (recommend ...) [link]` subject got its `D1`/`D2` label, so the labelling hook was active then.

## Effect seen

After the reload the task list no longer held the D items the session had created (`TaskUpdate` on task 2 returned "Task not found"), so the decision record for the session was lost from the queue and survives only in the session transcript and the user's memory notes.

## To investigate

- How the hook chain is ordered when `cc-plugin-sec-default` is present, and what "sent the event on past it" means for a classic hook declared later in the chain: is the event consumed, or forwarded in a form the classic hook no longer matches?
- Whether this is specific to `/reload-plugins` (hooks re-registered in a different order) or applies from a fresh start as well.
- Whether the plugin should declare its hooks in the form `cc-plugin-sec-default` passes through, or declare an ordering/dependency on it.
- Whether a skipped Stop hook can leave open D/A items unflagged at turn end (the Stop hook is what reminds about unqueued actions).

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.289, Linux, background job session (`claude bg-spare`)
- plugins loaded: 23 plugins, 75 skills, 9 agents, 3 hooks, 3 plugin MCP servers, 5 plugin LSP servers (per `/reload-plugins` output)
- session-decisions 2026.10.20.2 (loaded), 2026.10.23.1 (in cache)

On Claude Code 2.1.289 the pane drew empty: the `[more]` Button's Text child is refused there, and the refusal took the whole pane tree with it ([#119](https://github.com/lokkju/skills/issues/119)). I bisected the published builds with `claude plugin test`: 2.1.294 and older refuse the child, 2.1.295 and newer accept it.

What changed:

- **Minimum Claude Code.** `hooks/version.ts` declares `MIN_CLAUDE_CODE = '2.1.300'`. The manifest schema has no field for a minimum host version (`metadata` is free-form and Claude Code doesn't read it), so the plugin checks `$.session.version()` at session start. On an older build, or one whose version it can't read, it shows a 20-second toast and a transcript line naming the version it needs, adds a SessionStart context note telling the model it's off and to number items itself, registers no command or tools, and every hook passes straight through. The pane, footer, labels and checks are off rather than half working.
- **Contained cards.** Each pane card is built inside a try. An element the host refuses as it's made (the 2.1.289 failure was thrown at JSX construction) now costs that card, which draws as a plain line, rather than the pane. A tree the host refuses after the hook returns can't be caught from the module; the engine has no per-element boundary.
- **CI.** The session-decisions tests run as a matrix on the minimum (read from `hooks/version.ts`) and on `@latest`; validation runs on `@latest` in place of the 2.1.300 pin.
- **AGENTS.md** has a "Minimum Claude Code" section: declare it, raise it to use newer features, refuse loudly below it, test at it in CI. The README's Requirements names the minimum.
- Removed the stray tracked `docs/demo.gif,`.

The `[more]` Button keeps its accent Text child, since every build at or above the minimum accepts it.

response.body:
## What happens

On Claude Code 2.1.289 the decisions pane opens and draws nothing once any open item has a `[more]` control. The footer count, `/decisions`, `decision_list` and the task files are all correct; only the pane is blank.

The engine refuses the pane's tree and skips the render hook:

```
session-decisions's ui.render hook was skipped: session-decisions: HooksError:
JSX element <Button key="more-D1"> takes one string child, its label, or none
```

## Cause

a03f077 ("draw [more] in the accent color, underlined") changed the `[more]` control in `hooks/register.tsx` from

```tsx
<Button key={`more-${item.label}`} plain dimColor label={MORE} hover={{ bold: true }} onPress={more} />
```

to a Button wrapping a Text element:

```tsx
<Button key={`more-${item.label}`} plain label={MORE} hover={{ bold: true }} onPress={more}>
  <Text color={ACCENT} underline>{MORE}</Text>
</Button>
```

On 2.1.289 `ButtonProps` has `label`, `plain`, `dimColor`, `variant`, `hotkey`, `hover` and `onPress`; a Button takes one string child or none, and has no resting `color` or `underline` prop. The refusal takes the whole pane tree down, not just the one button, so every card disappears.

This box is behind: current Claude Code is 2.1.309, and the plugin's comments already describe 2.1.300 behaviour, so the release was presumably developed on a build where a Button accepts a Text child. That is a guess until someone confirms the element contract on 2.1.309; I have not checked it.

## Evidence

`claude plugin test` against the installed caches, both on 2.1.289:

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 2026.10.23.1 | 111 pass, 17 fail, every failure the Button refusal above |
| 2026.10.20.2 | 121 pass, 0 fail |

The refusal line only reaches the transcript while the plugin folder is hot-reloading; in an ordinary session it goes to the debug log alone, so a user on an older build sees an empty pane and nothing else.

## What should change

Two things, independent of which build is "right":

1. **A minimum-version check or a feature gate.** The plugin should either declare the Claude Code version it needs and say so (a toast at `session.start`, and ideally a manifest field if the host honours one), or probe for the capability it depends on and fall back when it is missing. For this case the fallback is the 2026.10.20.2 button: `plain dimColor label={MORE}`, with `hover={{ color: ACCENT, underline: true, bold: true }}` to keep the accent look where the host supports it. A `ui.render` hook that throws must not take the whole pane with it; wrap the risky element so the rest of the tree still draws.

2. **Test on the oldest build the plugin claims to support, or pin the claim.** The release's own suite catches this on 2.1.289 in under four seconds. Running `claude plugin test` in CI against the minimum supported Claude Code version, not only the developer's current one, would have blocked the release.

## Workaround

`claude plugin install session-decisions@lokkju@2026.10.20.2`, or update Claude Code to 2.1.309 if the element contract there does accept the child (unverified).

Skills called their bundled scripts as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/...`. That variable only exists in Claude Code's plugin runtime, so a skill loaded any other way (OpenCode pointed at a clone, `npx skills add`, a plain `~/.claude/skills` entry) ran `/scripts/...` and failed.

## What I chose

**The scripts move into the skill's own directory.** Each plugin's `scripts/` (with its Python package) is now `skills/<skill>/scripts/`, and term-recorder's `examples/` is now `skills/term-recorder/examples/`. I checked what `npx skills add` does (skills 1.7.4, `copyDirectory`): it copies only the directory holding `SKILL.md`. A `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<skill dir>/../..}` fallback would keep working for a clone but would still point at nothing after `npx skills add`, so moving the files is the only option that covers every install path the issue names.

**SKILL.md names them as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/<name>`.** Claude Code 2.1.306 replaces `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` with the skill's directory in the skill body and in `allowed-tools`. Each SKILL.md now says, in one line, that `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` is the directory holding the SKILL.md and that an agent which leaves it as written should put that directory's path in its place. forge-release already said its paths are relative to the skill's directory.

**Hooks and commands keep `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, pointed at the new location (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<skill>/scripts/<name>`). `hooks/hooks.json` and `commands/*.md` only run in Claude Code's plugin runtime, where the variable is always set, so they don't need the fallback.

## Verified on screen

I drove Claude Code 2.1.306 with term-recorder itself: `claude --model haiku --permission-mode default --plugin-dir plugins/term-recorder`, with the installed copy switched off, asked to run the skill's script. The skill loaded ("1 tool allowed"), the model ran `/…/plugins/term-recorder/skills/term-recorder/scripts/term-record -C … -s … -o … -- bash -c 'echo hello; sleep 3'` with the absolute path filled in, and it ran with no permission prompt in manual mode. So the `allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/term-record *)` grant still matches. (When the model chained a `mkdir -p … &&` in front, Claude Code did prompt, as it would have before; the grant covers the script, not the chain.)

## Also changed

- Tests, `ruff.toml`'s extensionless entry points, the plugin READMEs, `AGENTS.md` (layout, plus a paragraph on where skill scripts live and which variable to use where) and `docs/specs/forge-tracker.md` follow the new paths.
- forge-tracker's SKILL.md fallback to raw `gh api` calls was introduced as "Without the plugin (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` unset…)"; the script now ships with the skill, so it reads "Where the script can't run".

## Checks

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on all plugins.
- pytest: forge-release 89, forge-tracker 481, term-recorder 24, worktree-tidy 61, all pass.
- `claude plugin validate --strict` on the marketplace and each of the four plugins, and `scripts/check-skill-names.py`.

Closes #118

## Problem

Several skills invoke their bundled scripts via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, which is only defined when the plugin is loaded through the Claude Code **plugin** runtime. Discovered any other way — e.g. OpenCode's `skills` config pointing at a clone of this repo, a direct `~/.claude/skills` entry, or any non-Claude harness — the variable expands to empty and every invocation breaks:

```bash
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/term-recorder/scripts/rec.py …
# becomes: python3 /skills/term-recorder/scripts/rec.py  →  No such file
```

## Affected files (at HEAD)

`git grep -c 'CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT' HEAD -- '*.md'`:

- `plugins/forge-release/skills/forge-release/SKILL.md` + `references/yeet-setup.md`
- `plugins/forge-tracker/commands/{catchup,groom,next}.md` + `skills/forge-tracker/SKILL.md`
- `plugins/term-recorder/skills/term-recorder/SKILL.md` + `README.md`
- `plugins/worktree-tidy/skills/worktree-tidy/SKILL.md`

The scripts themselves are self-contained (only stdlib Python + tmux/socket), so the absolute-path prefix is the only portability barrier.

## Suggested fix

Anchor script paths to the skill's own location instead of the plugin root:

- Say "run `scripts/rec.py` **relative to this SKILL.md's directory**" — every current harness resolves the skill base directory when it loads a SKILL.md, and the plugin-relative form happens to keep working in Claude Code too.
- Or define the fallback convention in the docs: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}`-style guidance per call site.

## Current workaround

In my OpenCode setup I rewrote the paths in the two affected in-use skills (`forge-release`, `term-recorder`) to the clone's absolute paths — works, but pins the checkout location and diverges from upstream.

- GitLab issue references render as `-/work_items/N`.
- The tests in `tests/forge.test.ts` and `tests/queue.test.ts` that pin `/-/issues/` are updated.
- A test pins the new path.
- The README's example link matches.

response.body:
Two changes to worktree-tidy, both approved after the first real sweep.

**In-use guard.** Before a linked worktree (or an orphan directory under `.claude/worktrees/` or `.wt/`) is judged, the scan checks whether something is using it. If anything is, it goes to a new "in use" list with the evidence and gets no removal command:

- this session's working directory, and locked worktrees with their lock reason (both were skipped silently before; Claude Code locks the worktrees its sessions and agents are in, so this is what surfaces them);
- a process other than the scanner whose cwd is inside it, named by pid and command. Linux reads `/proc/*/cwd` once per scan and skips entries it can't read; without `/proc` it asks `lsof -d cwd -Fpcn`; if neither works the report and hook say the check couldn't run instead of assuming the worktree is free;
- a Claude Code transcript changed within `--session-hours` (default 24, `WORKTREE_TIDY_SESSION_HOURS` for the hook): `~/.claude/projects/<encoded path>/<session>.jsonl`, named by session id and age, and agent transcripts under `…/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, whose `.meta.json` records `worktreePath`. Agents given a worktree write there rather than under the worktree's own encoded path, so without this they'd never match. The subagent index is built once per scan.

The new code is in `scripts/worktree_tidy/inuse.py`; `scan()` takes `proc_root` and `projects` so the tests use a fake `/proc` and a fake projects folder.

**Merged with the branch still on the remote is stale.** It used to go to "look at". It now counts as stale under the same conditions as before (clean, its commit in the PR, no open PR), and the why-text says `branch still on the remote`. A closed PR whose branch is still on the remote stays in "look at".

The scan.py docstring, README and skill describe both. Tests cover fake-`/proc` hits (including a subdirectory, an unreadable entry and the scanner's own pid), a real `sleep` child on Linux, session and subagent transcripts in and out of the window, the lsof parser, the check-couldn't-run note, locked and current worktrees, and the three remote-branch cases.

Against `/home/lokkju/projects/skills` (52 linked worktrees): 41 stale (40 merged, 1 detached), 1 to look at, 8 in use, including `term-recorder` (locked, its `claude` process, a session written 4 minutes earlier) and the agent worktrees active in the last day.

Refs #109
response.title: feat(worktree-tidy): leave in-use worktrees alone; merged with remote branch is stale
